papers.title: The spatiotemporal ecosystem of gallbladder cancer: From inflamed areas to invasive margins - Integrating biomechanical injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor lineages, and spatial niches.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is usually described as the end point of chronic cholelithiasis-associated inflammation, and yet this linear formulation does not explain why only a small fraction of people with gallstones develop cancer, why histologically similar precursor lesions follow different evolutionary routes, or why invasion preferentially advances through anatomically and immunologically distinct interfaces. We propose a spatiotemporal ecosystem model that links five domains: gallstones and reflux as precipitating conditions; bile as a chemically active habitat; resident or transient micro
papers.summary: This review proposes a spatiotemporal ecosystem model for gallbladder cancer that integrates five interconnected domains: gallstone/reflux injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor cell lineages, spatial immune niches, and biomechanical injury at invasive margins. The authors argue that this framework better explains why only a fraction of gallstone patients develop cancer and why histologically similar precursor lesions follow divergent evolutionary routes.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis of jaw-bone periosteum identifies the role of macrophage-derived SPP1 in Ctsk+Fmod+ periosteal cells.
papers.abstract: Periosteal cells (PCs) play a crucial role in bone regeneration. Currently, the spatial landscapes of jaw-bone periosteum during bone grafting remains unclear. In this study, we propose a modified guided bone regeneration (GBR) model and integrate single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) to dissect its spatial characteristics. We identify a functional subset of Ctsk+Fmod+ PCs within the jaw-bone periosteum of rat and human. In addition, we describe a spatial niche around the bone graft substitute, characterized by massive infiltration of macrophages interacting w
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular landscape of jaw-bone periosteum during guided bone regeneration in a modified rat model. The authors identify a functional Ctsk+Fmod+ periosteal cell subset and show that macrophage-derived SPP1 signals to these cells within a spatial niche surrounding the bone graft substitute, highlighting a key macrophage-periosteal cell interaction in bone healing.

papers.title: OT-knn: A neighborhood-aware optimal transport framework for aligning spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression while preserving spatial context within tissues, enabling detailed characterization of tissue organization. As ST technologies advance, aligning datasets across tissue sections, individuals, platforms, and developmental stages has become increasingly important but remains challenging due to sparse expression, biological heterogeneity, and geometric distortions between slices. We introduce OT-knn, a method for ST alignment that integrates local neighborhood information within an optimal transport framework. Rather than relying solely on sing
papers.summary: OT-knn is a new computational method for aligning spatial transcriptomics datasets that incorporates local neighborhood information into an optimal transport framework. This approach addresses common challenges in spatial data alignment such as sparse gene expression, biological heterogeneity, and geometric distortions between tissue sections. The method aims to improve cross-section, cross-individual, and cross-platform comparisons in spatial transcriptomics studies.

papers.title: Integrating AI-Based Digital Pathology with Spatial Transcriptomics for Deeper Insight.
papers.abstract: Histopathology preserves tissue architecture, whereas spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression within its native spatial context. Integrating these modalities with artificial intelligence (AI) can link morphology to spatial molecular states and scale spatial discoveries to routine pathology cohorts. Early hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-spatial models demonstrated the feasibility of local gene-expression prediction. However, transcriptome-wide reconstruction remains constrained by gene-specific predictability, molecular sparsity, image quality, platform heterogeneity, and limited genera
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining AI-based digital pathology with spatial transcriptomics can link tissue morphology to spatial gene expression patterns, enabling spatial discoveries to be scaled to routine pathology cohorts. While early H&E-to-spatial models show feasibility for local gene-expression prediction, transcriptome-wide reconstruction remains limited by gene-specific predictability, molecular sparsity, image quality, platform heterogeneity, and limited generalizability.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify LMX1B as a tumor suppressor orchestrating the GDF15-ATP4B axis in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is characterized by profound inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity and extensive tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, yet the spatially resolved cellular programs and intercellular communication networks orchestrating malignant progression remain poorly defined. LMX1B, a LIM homeodomain transcription factor essential for kidney morphogenesis, has not been previously investigated in renal carcinogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map cellular programs and intercellular communication in renal cell carcinoma, identifying the transcription factor LMX1B as a tumor suppressor. LMX1B appears to act through a GDF15-ATP4B signaling axis, revealing a previously unrecognized regulatory mechanism in kidney cancer progression.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike existing frameworks that rely on simulated data, it uses real biological data to evaluate DTU detection, aiming to provide more realistic and unbiased performance assessments.

papers.title: STCGCar: Graph Contrastive Learning with Reliable Augmentation for Spatial Transcriptomics Clustering.
papers.abstract: Accurately identifying spatial domains based on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data can greatly promote our understanding of cellular composition and tissue organization. While graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown significant advancements in spatial clustering, they tend to be insensitive to noisy edges, leading to intersections among identified spatial domains. Here, we introduce a GNN-based ST Clustering framework, called STCGCar, utilizing a Graph Contrastive learning model with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction strategies. The framework begins by creating an enhanced view thr
papers.summary: STCGCar is a graph neural network framework for clustering spatial transcriptomics data into spatial domains. It uses graph contrastive learning with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction to make clustering more robust to noisy edges, which typically cause spatial domains to blur into each other. The approach aims to improve identification of cellular composition and tissue organization from spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Disentangling the cellular composition of FLCN-mutated tumors in Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome by spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome is a hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the folliculin (FLCN) gene and is associated with an increased risk of multifocal renal tumors. FLCN-mutated tumors (FMTs) often exhibit morphological heterogeneity with mixed morphological features resembling renal oncocytoma (RO) and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC), yet the molecular basis underlying the heterogeneous morphologic features and the morphologic-genomic correlations remain poorly defined. In our prior work, we identified mutually exclusive expressions of L1 cell
papers.journal: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to dissect the cellular composition of kidney tumors arising in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, which are driven by FLCN mutations and often show mixed features resembling both oncocytoma and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma. The work aims to link the morphological heterogeneity of these tumors to underlying molecular and cellular differences, potentially clarifying how distinct cell populations contribute to the mixed histology.

papers.title: A Molecularly Anchored Spatial Transcriptomic Framework for Precise CA1-Subiculum Parcellation and Region-Resolved Analysis in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: The precise molecular delineation of the interface between the Subiculum (Sub) and cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) is a challenge in hippocampal research, as conventional cytoarchitectural boundaries are often ambiguous and limit reproducible regional annotation. Here, we developed a molecularly anchored spatial transcriptomic framework to define CA1-Sub regional identities using high-definition spatial transcriptomics (Stereo-seq) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) references.
papers.summary: This study introduces a spatial transcriptomics framework that uses Stereo-seq and single-nucleus RNA-seq to molecularly define the boundary between the CA1 and Subiculum regions of the hippocampus, which is often ambiguous using traditional anatomy. The approach enables more precise, reproducible regional annotation and region-resolved analysis in Alzheimer's disease research.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics reveals OAT-associated arginine-proline metabolic remodeling in Paraquat-induced Parkinsonian and depression-like phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is a highly toxic bipyridyl herbicide that remains in agricultural use in some regions despite bans or severe restrictions elsewhere and is also widely used as a model toxicant for investigating environmentally induced neurodegeneration. However, the spatial metabolic alterations associated with PQ-induced neurobehavioral impairment remain incompletely understood. In this study, we performed AFADESI-MSI-based spatial metabolomic profiling and Visium spatial transcriptomic profiling on PQ-exposed mouse brains, and integrated these analyses with targeted metabolite assays, molecula
papers.summary: This study combines spatial metabolomics (AFADESI-MSI) and spatial transcriptomics (Visium) to map metabolic and gene expression changes in mouse brains exposed to the herbicide paraquat, a model toxicant for Parkinson's disease. The authors identify OAT-associated arginine-proline metabolic remodeling that accompanies paraquat-induced Parkinsonian and depression-like behavioral phenotypes. The work links a specific metabolic pathway to neurobehavioral impairment in an environmental toxicity model.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to the environmental pollutant 1-nitropyrene causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice, with extravillous trophoblasts identified as a key affected cell type. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with the Scissor machine learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint core regulatory targets underlying trophoblast dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses genetic multiplexing to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, revealing cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics. It extends and verifies prior single-cell RNA-seq findings by characterizing molecular subtypes of these neurons with complementary approaches.

papers.title: Spatial and single-cell dissection of medulloblastoma identifies developmental hierarchies and a prognostic PPIA-BSG tumor-immune axis.
papers.abstract: Medulloblastoma (MB) in children is highly heterogeneous, leading to its classification into molecular subgroups and resulting in significant differences in clinical outcomes even within the same risk group. This heterogeneity severely hampers the clinical management of MB. Therefore, it is essential to characterize MB heterogeneity within its tumor microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial and single-cell transcriptomics to dissect the cellular heterogeneity and developmental hierarchies within medulloblastoma tumors. The authors identify a PPIA-BSG tumor-immune axis that correlates with patient prognosis, offering a potential biomarker for stratifying outcomes within molecular subgroups.

papers.title: Multi-omics and experimental validation identify RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (KIRC) is characterized by marked molecular heterogeneity and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers for prognostic assessment and individualized treatment. RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor has been implicated in cell adhesion and differentiation, but its role in KIRC remains unclear. In this study, we systematically evaluated the expression pattern, prognostic significance, genomic associations, biological function, and therapeutic relevance of RAPGEF2 in KIRC through integrated multi-omics analyses and experimenta
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, is downregulated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and its lower expression is associated with worse patient prognosis. The authors propose RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker with potential therapeutic relevance in KIRC.

papers.title: TRPV1-STAT3 signaling as a driver of lethal pathology during pneumococcal nose-to-brain invasion.
papers.abstract: Nose-to-brain infection represents a non-hematogenous route by which pathogens invade the central nervous system via neural pathways. The olfactory and trigeminal systems are implicated in this process, but the molecular mechanisms underlying lethal pathology remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that trigeminal TRPV1 and downstream STAT3 signaling contribute to disease progression during pneumococcal nose-to-brain infection. A murine intranasal infection model using Streptococcus pneumoniae was established with methimazole-induced olfactory epithelial damage and/or resiniferatoxin-m
papers.summary: This study investigates how Streptococcus pneumoniae invades the brain via the nose-to-brain route, focusing on the trigeminal nerve. The authors show that TRPV1 and downstream STAT3 signaling drive lethal pathology in a mouse intranasal infection model, suggesting these pathways as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillations and identifies target genes of the Hes family of transcription factors, which are downstream effectors of Notch signaling. The tool addresses the challenge of experimentally tracking individual Hes target genes by using computational reconstruction instead of costly bioluminescence imaging. This enables broader identification of oscillating genes involved in cell fate decisions across multiple tissue types.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe). Instead of choosing a single method or averaging all methods, the classifier learns edge-specific weights, and the authors also provide a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated genes that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The findings suggest that lactate metabolism and lactylation play a role in HIRI and could serve as potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to predict survival and immunotherapy response. Low-PIS patients showed better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 was validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments. The work nominates ADAM12 and the PIS as potential biomarkers for stratifying NSCLC immunotherapy.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma, identifying four hub genes including TUBA1C. In vitro experiments validated TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target, and the signature was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature associated with tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The authors link this TDT-related signature to prognosis and propose potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. The work suggests that tumor growth kinetics have a measurable molecular basis that could inform patient stratification.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing, using paired short-read and long-read datasets. The authors systematically compare methods for isoform detection and alternative splicing analysis, providing guidance on tool performance for full-length transcript coverage in single-cell contexts.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors, such as a third-order drug-response tensor combined with a second-order transcriptomics matrix. It combines group factor analysis and tensor decomposition to learn interpretable latent factors, addressing a gap in existing integration methods that cannot handle heterogeneous tensor orders.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: sPYce is a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without requiring sequence alignment, addressing a gap since existing methods were designed for single-cell gene expression data and perform poorly on chromatin accessibility. It enables direct comparison of gene regulatory elements and regulatory programmes between species, offering new insight into how regulatory divergence contributes to differences in cell identity and phenotype.

papers.title: COL1A1+ Epithelial Cells Orchestrate VEGFA-VEGFR Signaling in Endometritis Revealed by Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometritis is linked to adverse reproductive outcomes, but epithelial programs in disease initiation and persistence remain unclear. We aimed to systematically define inflammation-associated epithelial states and regulation in endometritis using single-cell analysis.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell analysis to characterize epithelial cell states in endometritis, identifying a COL1A1+ epithelial population that appears to drive VEGFA-VEGFR signaling during inflammation. The findings suggest this epithelial subset may play a central role in disease initiation and persistence, offering potential targets for understanding endometritis pathology.

papers.title: microRNAs as Regulators of the Immune Response and Their Potential Therapeutic Applications in Cancer.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that have emerged as critical regulators of gene expression and key cellular processes in cancer, including tumor cell proliferation, survival, metastasis, and both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. Through their ability to modulate immune cell development, differentiation, polarization, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling and immune checkpoint expression, miRNAs play a vital role in shaping immune responses and represent attractive therapeutic candidates for remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Th
papers.summary: This review examines how microRNAs regulate both innate and adaptive immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, influencing immune cell development, polarization, antigen presentation, and immune checkpoint expression. It highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting or delivering miRNAs to remodel the tumor immune microenvironment in cancer treatment.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning and multimodal single cell analysis link NR4A2 to CD8+ T-cell terminal exhaustion and a CD8-adjusted prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Terminal exhaustion of CD8+ tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes constrains the benefit of immune-checkpoint blockade in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The orphan nuclear receptor NR4A2 (Nurr1) belongs to a transcription-factor family implicated in murine T-cell exhaustion, yet its behaviour in the human HCC microenvironment has not been characterised across data modalities. We asked whether NR4A2 is specifically coupled to the terminal-exhaustion programme of human HCC CD8+ T cells, and whether that coupling is reflected in chromatin, tissue topography and bulk-tumour outcome data.
papers.summary: This study uses explainable machine learning combined with multimodal single-cell analysis to show that the transcription factor NR4A2 is specifically linked to terminal exhaustion of CD8+ T cells in hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors further develop a CD8-adjusted prognostic signature, connecting NR4A2-driven exhaustion to patient outcomes. The work spans chromatin, spatial tissue data, and bulk tumor data to characterize NR4A2's role in the human HCC microenvironment.

papers.title: Ten quick tips for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while retaining spatial context within tissue sections. Since the foundational work by Ståhl et al. in 2016, the field has expanded rapidly, with diverse platforms now spanning sequencing-based (e.g., Visium, Visium HD, Slide-seq, Stereo-seq, and Seq-Scope) and imaging-based (e.g., MERFISH, Xenium, and CosMx SMI) approaches. The breadth of platforms, data structures, and computational tools, however, can be daunting for newcomers. Here, we present ten quick tips spanning the entire ST research workflow: whether ST suits
papers.summary: This paper provides ten practical tips for researchers new to spatial transcriptomics, covering the full workflow from experimental design through data analysis. It addresses the rapidly growing landscape of sequencing-based and imaging-based platforms, helping newcomers navigate the complexity of platform choice, data structures, and computational tools.

papers.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics of irradiated submandibular glands treated with fortified fibrin hydrogels.
papers.abstract: Previous studies showed that fortified fibrin hydrogel (Ep-FH), generated by conjugating laminin-1 peptides (A99 and YIGSR) and growth factors (FGF7 and FGF10) to fibrin hydrogels, improves epithelial organization and secretory function in irradiated mouse submandibular glands (SMG). To define the cell type-specific mechanisms underlying these effects, we generated high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiles using the Xenium Prime Mouse Pan Tissue and Pathways Panel (5,000 genes). Treatment with Ep-FH partially reactivated secretory- and polarity-related genes, shifted stromal and immune t
papers.summary: This study uses high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Xenium Prime Mouse Pan Tissue panel, 5,000 genes) to dissect how a fortified fibrin hydrogel (Ep-FH) improves epithelial organization and secretory function in irradiated mouse submandibular glands. The treatment partially reactivated secretory- and polarity-related genes and shifted stromal and immune cell populations, revealing cell type-specific mechanisms of gland recovery.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the ribosomal protein RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify Bregs and RPS2 as potential drivers of metastasis, suggesting they may serve as therapeutic targets to prevent bone metastasis in NPC patients.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and therapy resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and the formation of immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify cellular senescence programs in skin cutaneous melanoma, then uses machine-learning screening to build a senescence-based prognostic signature. The model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, suggesting senescence-related gene programs can stratify patient outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal LYZ and ISG15 as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CKD represents a substantial worldwide health challenge, defined by the gradual development of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced renal performance. Autoimmune-mediated factors are central to this pathological process, yet early diagnostic biomarkers and specific therapeutic targets are scarce. The objective of this research is to systematically pinpoint crucial specific genes that contribute to autoimmune-mediated CKD progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify LYZ and ISG15 as key genes involved in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease (CKD). The authors propose these genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for early detection and treatment of CKD.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify natural killer (NK) cell-related hub genes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and builds a two-gene risk model for diagnosis. The authors validate this model as a potential tool for distinguishing COPD patients, highlighting NK cell involvement in disease pathology.

papers.title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders (DD) are highly heterogeneous psychiatric illnesses. Their complex pathogenesis, coupled with suboptimal response rates to current clinical treatments, poses significant challenges to global mental health. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of DD at the transcriptomic level. This paper reviews recent advances utilizing bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), and single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) to explore the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), perinatal depression (PND), per
papers.summary: This review surveys recent applications of bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing to study the molecular pathogenesis of depressive disorders, including major depressive disorder and perinatal depression. It highlights how transcriptomic approaches reveal cellular heterogeneity and dysregulated pathways underlying these conditions, while also discussing ongoing technical and analytical challenges.

papers.title: Single-cell Raman profiling of B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation with transcriptome inference.
papers.abstract: Label-free profiling of cellular transcriptional and metabolic states during B cell differentiation and malignant transformation remains technically challenging. Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive alternative for single-cell biochemical characterization, yet its ability to infer transcriptomic profiles and distinguish leukemic cells has been limited.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell Raman spectroscopy to profile B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation in a label-free, non-destructive manner, and attempts to infer transcriptomic states from the Raman spectral data. The work suggests Raman profiling can distinguish leukemic from normal B cells and may serve as a proxy for transcriptional/metabolic state without needing labels or destructive assays.

papers.title: From transcriptomic profiling to precision oncology: a bibliometric analysis of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become an important tool for investigating the molecular heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); however, the global development and thematic evolution of this field remain inadequately characterized.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia, examining publication trends, key contributors, and thematic evolution over time. It aims to characterize how transcriptomic profiling has progressed toward precision oncology applications in AML, though the abstract provides only the study's rationale rather than specific findings.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates peripheral blood cell patterns in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy. By combining pharmacovigilance data with single-cell analysis, the authors aim to identify early markers of severe (fulminant) cases and characterize the immune cell changes in the blood that accompany this condition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model that exhibits both proximal and distal epithelial features, addressing a key limitation of existing lung organoid models that capture only single epithelial lineages. This model enables endogenous integration of multiple pulmonary cell types and is intended for studying idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis mechanisms and drug screening.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk to a specific JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program that shows high transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche analysis, and machine learning-based selection, the authors identify a pathogenic immune cell state linking genetic susceptibility to peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis in PSC.

papers.title: Circulating and tumor-infiltrating immune cell profiles in cervical cancer checkpoint blockade: multi-omics biomarkers of response and resistance.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has changed the therapeutic landscape of cervical cancer, but clinical benefit remains heterogeneous and difficult to predict with single biomarkers. Cervical cancer is a particularly suitable setting for immune-cell profiling because HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy-induced tissue remodeling, anti-angiogenic combinations, and repeated exposure to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors all shape the blood-tumor immune axis. This Mini Review discusses how circulating immune cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells can be jointly interrogated by multi-omics technologies to i
papers.summary: This mini review discusses how combining circulating immune cell profiling with tumor-infiltrating immune cell analysis via multi-omics approaches can identify biomarkers predicting response or resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in cervical cancer. It highlights that HPV-driven antigenicity, chemoradiotherapy, anti-angiogenic combinations, and repeated PD-1/PD-L1 exposure all shape the blood-tumor immune axis, making single biomarkers insufficient. The review argues for integrated multi-omics strategies to better stratify patients.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for automated detection of interictal epileptiform discharges: methodological progress, clinical evaluation, and neurodevelopmental context.
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are established electroencephalographic biomarkers that support epilepsy diagnosis and characterization, but their visual identification is time-consuming and subject to inter-rater variability. This review critically examines automated IED analysis from rule-based systems to contemporary deep learning, with particular attention to task definition, validation design, and clinical workflow. We use the term "accuracy paradox" as an author-defined descriptive label-not as an established field-wide concept-for the mismatch between high performance on prese
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review surveys automated detection of interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in EEG, tracing the evolution from rule-based systems to modern deep learning approaches. It emphasizes methodological issues in task definition and validation design, and introduces the author-defined term "accuracy paradox" to describe the mismatch between high benchmark performance and real-world clinical utility. The paper also situates these tools within neurodevelopmental context and clinical workflow considerations.

papers.title: Integrated single cell transcriptomics analysis for unraveling heterogeneity and plasticity of root cells for sustainable and regenerative agriculture.
papers.abstract: The plant root system architecture (RSA) functions in anchorage, acquisition of water and mineral nutrients, and exhibits pronounced phenotypic plasticity in response to the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of the soil environment. Resolving the regulatory networks that underpin root development is therefore a prerequisite for improving stress tolerance and yield. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves transcriptional landscapes at cellular resolution, discriminating root zonation, lineage trajectories and cell-type-restricted responses to environmental signals. Coupling scRNA-seq to epig
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell RNA sequencing is being used to dissect the cellular heterogeneity and developmental plasticity of plant root systems, including root zonation, cell lineage trajectories, and cell-type-specific responses to soil environmental signals. It argues that resolving these regulatory networks is essential for engineering stress-tolerant, higher-yielding crops for sustainable and regenerative agriculture.

papers.title: Dynamic orchestration of structural and immune cells in acute Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia revealed by time-resolved single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia triggers a complex, dynamic host response, yet the cellular coordination of inflammation and repair remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses time-resolved single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map how structural and immune cells coordinate their responses during acute Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia. The authors reveal dynamic, stage-specific cellular interactions underlying inflammation and tissue repair. The work provides a detailed temporal atlas of the host response to this clinically important pathogen.

papers.title: Unraveling tumor cell heterogeneity and epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity in gastric adenocarcinoma: an integrative multi-omics framework evaluating PVR/CD155 as a tumor cell-intrinsic EMT-associated target.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) of gastric adenocarcinoma is exceptionally heterogeneous, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a central mechanism promoting local invasion and metastatic spread. Even so, how EMT-programmed cells are spatially arranged within tumor tissue, how they interact with neighboring immune populations, and which molecular nodes might be exploited therapeutically remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to characterize tumor cell heterogeneity and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) programs in gastric adenocarcinoma, mapping how EMT-like tumor cells are spatially organized and interact with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. The authors identify PVR/CD155 as a tumor cell-intrinsic EMT-associated molecule that could serve as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Single-cell lineage tracing in tumor organoids identifies expansion states depicting the origin and progression of lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Only a subset of epithelial cells can initiate progressive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the founder cell states that confer this competence remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell lineage tracing in tumor organoids to identify specific expansion states of epithelial cells that can initiate and drive lung adenocarcinoma progression. The findings suggest that only certain founder cell states are competent to give rise to progressive tumors, offering new insights into the cellular origins of LUAD.

papers.title: A parallel convolution attention network for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genome prediction is a breeding strategy that predicts crop phenotype through genomic markers. Traditional statistical models cannot accurately capture the complex relationships between genotypes and phenotypes, and deep neural networks have shown significant advantages in capturing nonlinear relationships. Deep learning methods in genome selection primarily utilize sequential convolutional kernels, which can lead to challenges such as gradient disappearance and computational inefficiency. In this study a novel crop genomic prediction method based on a parallel convolutional attention network
papers.summary: This paper introduces a parallel convolutional attention network for crop genomic prediction, aiming to improve on traditional statistical models and sequential convolutional deep learning approaches that suffer from gradient vanishing and computational inefficiency. The method is designed to better capture complex nonlinear relationships between genotypes and phenotypes for breeding applications.

papers.title: Engineered Exosomal miRNAs for Post-Stroke Neural Repair: Mechanisms, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Functional neurological recovery after ischemic stroke remains a formidable challenge in neuroscience. Exosomes serve as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication, and the microRNAs (miRNAs) they carry, in particular, offer a promising "cell-free therapy" strategy for promoting neurological repair. This review systematically summarizes the multi-target mechanisms by which exosomal miRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit (NVU) and outlines technical strategies to enhance exosomal therapeutic efficacy through targeted modification and engineered cargo loading, with the aim of constructing
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how exosomal microRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit after ischemic stroke and can be harnessed as a cell-free therapy to promote neural repair. It also surveys engineering strategies—such as targeted modification and engineered cargo loading—to improve delivery and therapeutic efficacy, while outlining remaining translational barriers.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics decoding of the fracture nonunion niche: from immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk to precision regeneration.
papers.abstract: Fracture nonunion - the failure of bone to heal without surgical intervention - affects 5%-10% of all fractures and represents a substantial clinical and economic burden. Despite decades of research, the cellular and molecular mechanisms that distinguish successful repair from nonunion remain incompletely understood, largely because the fracture niche is a spatially organized, multicellular ecosystem whose crosstalk cannot be captured by bulk analyses. The recent convergence of spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics, and computational integration methods has opene
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics) can decode the cellular and molecular ecosystem of fracture nonunion, a condition affecting 5-10% of fractures. It highlights immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk within the spatially organized fracture niche and proposes these approaches for developing precision regeneration strategies.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell analysis characterizes malignant epithelial programs and context-dependent immune associations of MP7/SERINC2 in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) comprises heterogeneous malignant epithelial states, but it remains unclear which transcriptional programs recur across patients and how these programs relate to the immune context.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated single-cell analysis to identify recurrent malignant epithelial transcriptional programs in colorectal cancer and examines how these programs relate to immune cell context. The authors specifically characterize the expression of MP7/SERINC2 across malignant states and find that its immune associations are context-dependent rather than uniform. This provides a framework for understanding how tumor cell heterogeneity shapes immune interactions in CRC.

papers.title: Spatially resolved gene expression analysis illuminates location-specific functions in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta.
papers.abstract: Reef-building coral polyps contain multiple specialized tissue types with distinct functions, from feeding and defense to symbiosis and skeleton formation. While these cell types have been characterized microscopically and more recently via single-cell RNA sequencing, spatially resolved high-throughput gene expression profiling remains limited in corals. Here we combine Laser Capture Microdissection with RNA sequencing to characterize tissue-specific gene expression in the reef building coral Pocillopora acuta. Oral tissues, adjacent to the seawater, exhibited 1,253 upregulated genes enriched
papers.summary: This study applies laser capture microdissection combined with RNA sequencing to profile tissue-specific gene expression in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta. The authors identify distinct transcriptional signatures across anatomically separated tissues, with oral tissues showing 1,253 upregulated genes enriched for functions related to their interface with seawater. The work provides a spatially resolved transcriptomic resource for corals, complementing existing single-cell studies.

papers.title: Network-informed deconvolution of bulk immune gene co-expression reveals single-cell programs and spatial organization.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has opened unprecedented possibilities to explore the complexity of the immune system. However, existing methods primarily rely on expression-based clustering analysis, which lacks mechanistic explanations for immune cell states and encounters challenges in integrating multi-scale data.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a network-informed deconvolution approach that leverages immune gene co-expression networks to extract single-cell programs from bulk RNA-seq data. This method aims to bridge bulk and single-cell data by revealing cell-state programs and their spatial organization, addressing limitations of expression-based clustering. It offers a mechanistic framework for interpreting immune cell states across scales.

papers.title: Spatial compartmentalization of melanoma cell states reveals CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key components of the melanoma tumor microenvironment and have been implicated in immune evasion and therapy resistance. However, the spatial relationships between CAFs, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and immune exclusion remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial profiling to map how cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) organize the melanoma tumor microenvironment, revealing distinct spatial compartments where CAF-associated tumor cells show enhanced proliferative capacity. The work links CAF proximity to ECM remodeling and immune exclusion, suggesting CAFs help create niches that support tumor growth and evade immune attack.
